facts.statement: Richard Lydekker named the genus and species Sarcolestes in 1893, initially believing it was a theropod.
facts.quote: The genus and species were named in 1893 by Richard Lydekker, who thought they belonged to a theropod.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Sarcolestes is a partial left mandible and a fused scute damaged during excavation.
facts.quote: The holotype and only specimen, is a partial left mandible and fused scute that was damaged during excavation (specimen NHMUK PV R 2682).

facts.statement: The preserved jaw contains one entire tooth and two crown tips, with the central section of the bone missing.
facts.quote: The jaw preserved one entire tooth and two crown tips in its alveolus, with the missing bone in the central section of the mandible.

facts.statement: Sarcolestes is one of the few known ankylosaurians from the Middle Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Sarcolestes is one of a few ankylosaurians known from the Middle Jurassic

facts.statement: Sarcolestes lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 162 million years ago in the Callovian stage in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 162 millones de años, en el Calloviense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Sarcolestes reached a length of approximately 3 meters.
facts.quote: que llegó a medir alrededor de los 3 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa classified Sarcolestes as a herbivorous stegosaurid in 1901.
facts.quote: In 1901, Franz Nopcsa found that Sarcolestes was in fact herbivorous, and classified it in Stegosauridae with genera such as Polacanthus, Stegosaurus, Hylaeosaurus, Stenopelix and various others.

facts.statement: Peter Galton concluded that Sarcolestes belongs to the nodosaurid family based on its dentary similarity to Sauropelta.
facts.quote: Peter Galton concluded that Sarcolestes represents a genus within Nodosauridae, with a dentary similar to that of Sauropelta.

facts.statement: Some researchers have questioned the classification of Sarcolestes within Nodosauridae and even its validity as a distinct genus.
facts.quote: However, others have cast doubt on this assignment and even the validity of Sarcolestes.

facts.statement: Sarcolestes is classified within the parent group Ankylosauria.
Sarcolestes belongs to the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
The time range for Sarcolestes is estimated between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Sarcolestes is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian ornithischian dinosaur named "flesh robber" after its Greek roots.
rejected.quote: Sarcolestes (from Ancient Greek σάρξ (sárx), meaning "flesh", and λῃστής (lēistḗs), meaning "robber", and thus, "flesh robber") is an extinct genus of ankylosaurian ornithischian dinosaur from the Oxford Clay of England.
